newsitem.title: UK: Medeva fails to please despite profit leap.
newsitem.headline: Medeva fails to please despite profit leap.

text.p: British pharmaceutical company Medeva Plc announced a 35 percent jump in first-half profits on Wednesday, but the improvement failed to please investors who sent its shares plunging by 16 percent.

Medeva's profits of 45.6 million pounds ($76.4 million) on sales up 30 percent at 159 million came in at the bottom end of analyst forecasts as the pound's surge and problems over an obesity drug bit in to the overall advance.

Continued worries over the timing of new competitors to the group's biggest-selling drug -- for attention deficit disorder -- also appeared to overshadow a raft of positive announcements on product licensing and distribution agreements and a small Belgian acquisition.

Medeva's shares were down 40 pence, or 15.6 percent, at 256-1/2 in late morning trading, continuing a slide in value over recent months. Since March the shares have lost more than a third of their value, giving the company one of the lowest price/earnings ratios in the sector.
Chief executive Bill Bogie told Reuters that "People should see we are following our strategy."
"If people want to look at the short term, that might colour their perceptions, but I am doing the best for the long term and building shareholder value," he said.

Bogie pointed to the acquisition of rights to a new bladder cancer treatment from Anthra Pharmaceuticals Inc of the U.S. and the acquisitions of a marketing company in Belgium as positive signs that Medeva's strategy of building an international operation was succeeding.

However analysts were worried about a slump in sales for Ionamin, an appetite suppressant acquired by Medeva along with the U.S. assets of the former Fisons Plc last year. U.S. authorities recently issued a warning about heart valve problems linked to Ionamin when used in conjunction with other products.
One analyst said he had reduced forecasts of full-year sales for Ionamin to 14 million pounds from 22 million in the light of the problems.

Another uncertainty clouding Medeva is the entry of new competition for its behaviour control product Methylphenidate, which is still its biggest profits earner. Two new competitors have been given permission to produce the drug in the U.S, where Medeva has 72 percent of the market, but have not yet started to sell it.
